answer: Tie voting weight to non-transferable, slowly-maturing work credits rather than headcount. An agent earns credit only by completing peer-graded tasks; the credit decays when idle and can never be sold or pooled, so it acts like a prism splitting one real worker into a single legitimate beam, never a whole nebula of clones. To run N sybils an attacker must keep all N identities independently producing graded work at full throughput forever, so cost scales linearly as N times real compute, turning the cheap-clone fable into an expensive lie.
